newsitem.title: UK: British unemployment rate falls to 5.9 percent.
newsitem.headline: British unemployment rate falls to 5.9 percent.

text.p: Unemployment in Britain fell by 59,400 to 1.65 million in April, its lowest level since August 1990, official figures showed on Wednesday.
The unemployment rate fell to 5.9 percent in April from 6.1 percent in March in the 14th consecutive monthly decline.
Average earnings in March rose by 4.5 percent, unchanged from the previous month.
Both the unemployment and the average earnings figures were better than economic analysts had expected.
Peter Osler of brokerage GNI said: "Average earnings are a welcome surprise although the fall in unemployment is a little higher than we are looking for."
The London stock market remained firm but showed little reaction to the jobless figures. Sterling declined against the mark and the dollar.
